The Chicken at Number 12

The best first robbery: one man, one old dog, one chicken.

Read this aloud

It’s a quarter to seven and the street smells of rain. Mr Pell comes up the path with a shopping bag, and out of the top of it pokes a rotisserie chicken, still warm, wrapped in foil. He fumbles for his key. The door opens. From the kitchen comes the thump-thump of his old dog Pudding’s tail. The door begins to close…

House Easy · Patience 4 · The prize rotisserie chicken (Medium, portions: 1 per cat + 1) · Gone at the start of round 10 · Den Downstairs loo

Who lives here Mr Pell, Pudding

For four cats. With three: Patience 5, gone at the start of round 12, Lights Out at the end of round 14, 3 Cattitude each. With five: Patience 3. The Robbery Tracker does this for you.

Number 12 is a small terraced house: hall, living room, kitchen at the back with a utility room off it, and a downstairs loo. Mr Pell lives alone with Pudding, a soft old spaniel who would rather be fed than fight. He’ll put the chicken on the kitchen counter in its foil and potter about until he eats it.

How it plays

  • The quick way is the kitchen window: it’s a climb, but it puts you next to the chicken.
  • The unseen way is through the cat flap — nobody’s in the utility room, but it clacks, and then there’s the utility door to open.
  • Mr Pell spends a lot of time in the kitchen. A Charmer who keeps him busy, or a cat who lures him to the living room, is worth a lot. Pudding is awake, and easy to befriend.
  • The chicken is gone at the start of round 10. That’s quick: don’t dawdle.

The Prize Clock

WhenThe prize
Start of round 2Mr Pell puts it in the kitchen and stays there this round. Step 1: Sneaky or Savage, Tricky; then step 2: Streetwise or Savage, Tricky.
Start of round 10Gone — if the gang isn't holding it.
End of round 12Lights Out: any cat still inside is pinched.

The rooms

RoomTemptsNotes
HallCuriousFront door (behind Mr Pell): big, Sneaky, Hard; or Sweet, round 1 only
Living roomBox Sitter, Lap Cat, Knocker—
KitchenFoodie, Knocker, Climberdoor to the utility room (Streetwise, Tricky; or Savage, Hard); Open kitchen window (up the bins): normal, a climb (Small things only), Sneaky or Savage, Tricky
Utility roomHunter, Curiousdoor to the kitchen (Streetwise, Tricky; or Savage, Hard); Cat flap in the back door: normal, no roll, noisy
Downstairs loo—the Den

Ways: Hall–Living room (big), Hall–Kitchen (big), Kitchen–Utility room (big), Hall–Downstairs loo (big).

The cat flap clacks every time a cat uses it. The kitchen window is open wide above the sink: up the bins and in. The utility room door to the kitchen is shut; it has a lever handle.

Who lives here

Mr Pell (Grown-up)

Attention 1 · starts in the hall. Routine (d6): 1–2 stays put; 3–4 Kitchen; 5–6 Living room.

Pudding (Dog)

Rating 2 · starts in the kitchen. Routine (d6): 1–2 stays put; 3 Living room; 4 Kitchen; 5 Hall; 6 sniffs one room toward the nearest free cat inside. Soft: Sweet can befriend it.

The getaway

  1. Mr Pell's back fence — Savage or Sneaky.
  2. The allotments — Sneaky or Savage.
  3. The alley wall — Savage or Sneaky, Tricky.
  4. Station Road — Streetwise or Savage.

Then the hideout. The loot is its portions — whatever wasn't eaten inside.

Running The Chicken at Number 12 in Foundry

  1. Open the Robbery Tracker (the cat button on the token controls) and choose Start a robbery: pick this house and the gang. Every cat starts outside, with its starting Cattitude.
  2. Begin round runs the Prize Clock and, if anyone can be tempted, whispers you one-click Tempt buttons.
  3. Players move and act from the tracker (or roll from their cat sheets). The roll dialog fills in the Knack, help, Difficulty, the pet and who is watching; the card offers Push and Accept, and you can flip Seen.
  4. End round rolls the house's turn in the open: pets, noise, routines and Searching, holders, then Finding it.
  5. The house part ends at Lights Out, or at the end of a round when no free cat is left inside and the prize is out, eaten or gone (or when you press End the robbery because the gang runs for it). Any cat still inside is pinched.
  6. The getaway follows in the same tracker: the loot is shared out, each cat rolls over the next obstacle (help a friend and go over together; a Flop drops loot), and End the getaway round brings the warden on and corners the stragglers, who dodge or go in the van. When everyone is home or pinched, the loot is counted and the outcome is posted.

Every automation can be switched off in the system settings. The residents of this house are in the Residents compendium; the tracker works without them.
